solution.title: Standardize Power Platform Secrets in Azure Key Vault

products.name: Standardize Power Platform Secrets in Azure Key Vault — Commercial
products.short_description: Standardize Power Platform secrets in Azure Key Vault — store API keys, client secrets, connection strings and certificates in the vault, retrieve them securely (Key Vault-backed Secret environment variables, the Azure Key Vault connector, or an Azure Function + managed identity), remove hardcoded credentials, and govern rotation. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Get every secret out of your Power Apps and flows — and into Azure Key Vault

Power Platform makes it far too easy to paste an API key into a flow, a client secret into a custom connector, or a connection string into an app formula — and once it's there, it leaks into run history, app definitions, logs, and exports, and it can't be rotated without rebuilding. This solution standardizes Power Platform secrets in Azure Key Vault: secrets live in the vault, apps and flows retrieve them securely through approved patterns, hardcoded credentials are removed everywhere, and rotation, ownership, and access are governed — so a key change never means an app rebuild.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — why secrets belong in Azure Key Vault, the secret types in scope (API keys, client secrets, connection strings, certificates, service-account credentials, external tokens), and the retrieval patterns for Power Platform — environment variables of type Secret (Key Vault-backed), the Azure Key Vault connector, and an Azure Function + managed identity via custom connector — with a decision guide for which to use.
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (an Azure subscription + Key Vault, Entra ID, the Power Platform environment and Dataverse, appropriate licensing, the Dataverse/Power Platform service principal, RBAC roles, network access) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.
  • Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: create/prepare the Key Vault, store the secrets, configure access with Entra ID RBAC / managed identities / service principals (grant the Dataverse app 'Key Vault Secrets User'), wire Power Platform to the vault (Secret environment variables and/or the connector/Function pattern), refactor apps/flows/connectors to stop using hardcoded secrets, validate no exposure, then pilot, validate, and expand.
  • Governance & rotation guidance — secret ownership, least-privilege access control, expiry/rotation policy, and how rotating a secret in the vault flows through to apps and flows without a rebuild.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — Key Vault + secret + RBAC discovery (and a hardcoded-secret risk scan of exported flow/app/connector definitions), access/retrieval validation (Dataverse SP has Key Vault Secrets User; Secret env vars resolve), a secrets inventory + expiry/rotation report, safe remediation (assign RBAC role, set expiry), and a rotation/ownership-tagging helper.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Every Power Platform secret centralized in Azure Key Vault, retrieved securely through approved patterns, with no hardcoded credentials left in apps, flows, connectors, or logs — and rotation that never requires an app rebuild, proven on a pilot before you scale.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • PPKV-Discovery.ps1 — inventory Key Vaults, secrets, and RBAC assignments, and scan exported
    • PPKV-Remediation.ps1 — safe remediation: assign 'Key Vault Secrets User' and set secret expiry
    • PPKV-Report.ps1 — secrets inventory with expiry/rotation and access report
    • PPKV-Set-RotationOwnership.ps1 — set rotation/expiry and ownership tags on Key Vault secrets
    • PPKV-Validation.ps1 — confirm the vault uses the RBAC model, the Power Platform service principal

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.

Government / GCC High tenant? A dedicated Government (GCC High) edition of this solution is available — authored for the US sovereign cloud (correct *.us portals, US Gov Graph endpoints, and Commercial-vs-GCC-High feature parity gaps called out).
